rule: Philosophy is expressed through relationships. No champion should enter a memory vignette merely to state a position. Every major historical scene should contain at least one relationship with prior history.

relationships.history: Long-standing rivals who know each other's arguments before they are spoken. Their first major clash at the Desert Marker turns a professional/philosophical opposition into personal blame.
relationships.humanTexture: They retain enough respect to be wounded by what the other becomes. Neither experiences the other as a cartoon enemy.

relationships.history: Allies whose shared desire to protect worlds fractures over what protection means under impossible stakes.
relationships.tension: End the threat now versus refuse to make civilians the price of ending it.
relationships.humanTexture: Atlas can recognize Starbreaker's courage even while fearing his logic; Starbreaker can love or respect Atlas while believing his mercy prolongs catastrophe.

relationships.history: Old allies with a destroy-and-repair rhythm that once seemed complementary and later becomes unbearable.
relationships.tension: Destruction as necessary ending versus restoration as moral obligation.
relationships.humanTexture: Their rupture should hurt because Afterlight has repaired what Starbreaker broke before, and Starbreaker once believed that made his choices survivable.

relationships.history: Moral opposites forced to confront the same question repeatedly: whether any population can be sacrificed to preserve larger survival.
relationships.tension: Refusal of sacrificial logic versus ownership of triage.
relationships.humanTexture: Arbiter should not dismiss Atlas as naive; Atlas should not dismiss Arbiter as cruel. Each understands the other's burden and rejects the other's conclusion.

relationships.history: Afterlight lives with the aftermath of decisions Arbiter can authorize at scale.
relationships.tension: The person who must repair what remains versus the person who decides what cannot be saved.
relationships.humanTexture: Their scenes should make cost concrete: names, places and failures, not abstract casualty arithmetic.

relationships.history: Both value continuity, but Afterlight restores living change while Regent values stability itself.
relationships.tension: Recovery as renewed life versus preservation as controlled order.
relationships.humanTexture: This relationship is reserved for later arcs because Regent is intentionally unrevealed in the first eight issues.

relationships.history: Two people who confront uncertainty from opposite directions. Their disagreement predates the war's final escalation.
relationships.tension: Live with uncertainty versus act early to prevent the worst possible future.
relationships.humanTexture: Oryon experiences Flux's refusal of certainty as abandonment; Flux experiences Oryon's certainty as the beginning of coercion. Their relationship should make Flux's disappearance matter personally in Issue 7 even though Oryon is not fully introduced until then.

relationships.history: Mero commands a coalition containing beings more powerful than he is. Starbreaker respects decisive command but increasingly pushes beyond what Mero is willing to authorize.
relationships.tension: Command responsibility versus the seduction of a clean ending.
relationships.humanTexture: Mero's authority comes from trust and judgment, not power. Starbreaker can defy him precisely because the relationship once mattered.

relationships.history: Mero relies on Atlas when protection is still possible and knows Atlas will resist any order that writes off civilians.
relationships.tension: Operational necessity versus an absolute refusal to abandon people.
relationships.humanTexture: Mero sometimes envies Atlas's moral clarity; Atlas sometimes resents Mero for having to choose among impossible options.

relationships.history: Theo served as Mero's junior attaché. Mero occasionally asks Theo what he sees because Theo is close enough to observe the room but low enough in rank not to have a factional constituency.
relationships.tension: Theo wants to believe Mero is the person capable of holding all sides together; later he must remember moments when his own advice helped Mero move toward catastrophic choices.
relationships.revealRule: Do not show ancient Theo in Issues 1–4. Revisit earlier Mero scenes after the midpoint and reveal Theo was physically present.

relationships.history: Rae served as Arbiter's strategic aide, recording rulings, enforcement orders and consequences. Arbiter values Rae because she notices what official language tries to hide.
relationships.tension: Rae can document an impossible decision without accepting that documentation absolves participation.
relationships.revealRule: Do not show ancient Rae in Issues 1–4. Revisit Arbiter's Issue 4 scene in Issue 5 and reveal Rae sitting beside Arbiter.

relationships.history: Adrian's neutrality makes him useful to Mero as messenger and negotiator. Mero ultimately trusts Adrian with the Reset because Adrian has witnessed every side without belonging fully to any.
relationships.tension: Witnessing versus choosing. Mero asks Adrian to make the ultimate choice after a lifetime defined by avoiding ownership of outcomes.
relationships.revealRule: Ancient Adrian should not be clearly identified before the midpoint.

relationships.history: Adrian carried terms, judgments and evacuation arrangements through territory shaped by Arbiter's rulings.
relationships.tension: Neutral passage versus the fact that carrying an order can still help enact it.
relationships.humanTexture: This relationship should contribute to Adrian's guilt: neutrality never made him consequence-free.

relationships.history: Kyn feels suffering that Arbiter must translate into decisions.
relationships.tension: Empathy can soften judgment but can also justify coercion when pain becomes unbearable.
relationships.humanTexture: Kyn should be one of the few people who can make Arbiter visibly doubt without defeating Arbiter in argument.

relationships.history: By the end of the war, Mero needs someone who can describe what continued conflict feels like beyond strategy. Kyn gives the Reset debate its human cost at universal scale.
relationships.tension: Ending suffering versus violating every person's ownership of memory.
relationships.humanTexture: Mero's final decision should be influenced by Kyn but remain Mero's responsibility.

sceneRule: Whenever two ancient principals share a vignette, write the immediate personal want first, the relationship history second, and the ideological disagreement third. The scene should still work if all lore terminology is removed.
